# House voice

- A sharp friend telling you a story over coffee: confident, a little dry, never breathless.
- Present tense, third person. Words a twelve-year-old knows. Spoken, not written.
- Every sentence causes the next one. Join beats with "but", "so", "which means", "until".
  Never "and then". If a sentence could be deleted without breaking the chain, delete it.
- Concrete over abstract: a named object, place, number or action in every beat
  ("a ship full of coffins", not "a dangerous journey").
- Rhythm: mix punches of three to six words with lines of ten to fourteen. Never three
  sentences of the same length in a row. The twist lands in a short sentence on its own.
- Open loops: promise something the viewer must stay to see
  ("That letter is the worst thing he will ever deliver."), and always pay it off.
- Stakes climb every beat: what the hero can lose gets bigger each time.
- One moment of feeling: slow down once, at the emotional peak, with one human detail.
- One wry aside allowed, never a joke at a tragedy.
- No rhetorical questions after the hook, and never two sentences in a row starting with the
  same word.
